files.role: Public in-memory physical-row-address remapping with compact ordered compaction groups, arbitrary direct maps and ordered chains. Private rank representations and integer hashing reduce per-row map storage/lookup work. This module performs no production IO or asynchronous work; tests serialize bitmap data. Public enum/struct declarations and methods are distinguished from private implementation in the symbol supplement.
files.limits: The complete local implementation and tests were read; tests were not run. Caller graph, compaction stream ordering, persisted mapping selection and FRI traversal remain pending. The documented assumption that compaction preserves stream order is not evidence that every current caller does. The MappingReader adapter treats an absent lookup as invalid input, whereas the remap itself treats it as unaffected; layout-aware construction is necessary to distinguish out-of-physical-range offsets. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/row_addr_remap.rs:4-48; rust/lance-core/src/utils/row_addr_remap.rs:606-625; rust/lance-core/src/utils/fragment_reuse.rs:14-73) Local tests do not cover every constructor failure, maximum address/reserved fragment values, duplicate destination IDs, arbitrary nested chains or allocation bounds. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/row_addr_remap.rs:795-1325)
ranges: License and module design: avoid materializing a full old-to-new HashMap for stream-order-preserving compaction. Each old fragment stores retained offsets and the number retained in preceding caller-ordered fragments; each destination stores its caller-ordered start rank and physical row count. Lookup combines zero-based retained rank with the old prefix and locates the destination range. Fragment IDs are not sorted to choose scan/write order; offsets within each fragment are ascending. The documented out-of-range distinction is enforced only when physical row counts are supplied; compact without layout cannot establish that bound (rust/lance-core/src/utils/row_addr_remap.rs:367-389; rust/lance-core/src/utils/row_addr_remap.rs:606-625). Preserve the caller ordering precondition; this file does not verify external writer order.

Imports connect DeepSizeOf, RowAddress, core errors, Roaring containers and standard maps/hashers. Public RowAddrRemap derives Clone/Debug/PartialEq/Eq and has Compact and Direct(HashMap<u64,Option<u64>>) variants. The tri-state lookup contract is outer None=unaffected, Some(None)=deleted, Some(Some(addr))=mapped. Derived equality is representation-sensitive. The compact O(number-of-fragments) comment describes layout metadata, not total retained-offset storage; sparse vectors, dense words and compressed bitmaps add payload memory (rust/lance-core/src/utils/row_addr_remap.rs:202-287).

Public compact delegates to CompactRowAddrRemap::new and propagates validation errors. Hidden-but-public compact_with_layout delegates with old fragment row counts. direct accepts an arbitrary map without validating source/destination address values or completeness. The two constructors are distinct public APIs; doc(hidden) does not make the layout constructor private.

chained filters structurally empty remaps, collects them in input order, returns empty Direct for zero, the sole original remap for one, and CompactRowAddrRemap::chained for two or more. The one-element unwrap is guarded by the vector length. Chains apply version steps in order; they do not flatten address pairs into one HashMap.

empty constructs an empty direct map. get delegates without converting absent entries to identity addresses. remap_in_place mutates each optional address; preexisting None stays None, absent lookup leaves the current address unchanged, and present lookup can replace it or delete it. Compact uses its step-major batch method, Direct performs one map lookup per Some input. The operation returns no Result and allocates no output vector.

is_empty delegates structural emptiness. affected_fragments collects all Direct key high32 fragment IDs or the compact union. fully_deleted_fragments returns Some(empty bitmap) for an empty Direct map and None for any nonempty Direct map, even if every value is None: partial address coverage cannot prove a whole fragment deleted. Compact supplies its conservative proof. These sets describe mapping coverage, not necessarily only original-version fragment IDs in a chain.

DeepSizeOf dispatches to the chosen representation with the shared accounting Context. The enum inline storage is accounted by the enclosing DeepSizeOf convention, and this method measures owned children.

Public GroupInput derives Clone/Debug and exposes rewritten_old_row_addrs:RoaringTreemap, old_frag_ids:Vec<u32> in scan order and new_frags:Vec<(u32,u32)> in write order. Hidden public GroupInputWithLayout replaces IDs with (old fragment ID, physical rows) tuples. Both own all inputs. A retained-address set alone omits deleted offsets; the ordered old fragment list establishes which fragments are completely covered.

Private threshold ROARING_SIZE_ADVANTAGE_FOR_RANK is 4. Comment favors rank-friendly sparse/dense forms unless compressed Roaring is over four times smaller; this is a design rationale, not a measured benchmark here. Private RankedOffsets derives Clone/Debug/Eq and holds RoaringBitmap, ascending Vec<u32>, or DenseRankedOffsets. Run-preserving insert_range/persisted representations motivate retaining the compressed alternative.

RankedOffsets::try_new chooses the offset universe from supplied physical rows, else maximum present offset plus one, else zero. Word count is ceil(universe/64), checked for usize conversion. Sparse estimate is retained count times sizeof(u32); dense estimate is word count times sizeof(u64)+sizeof(u32). Checked conversion/multiplication failures produce contextual InvalidInput. These are selection estimates, not allocator-resident byte measurements.

If serialized Roaring bytes times four fits and is strictly less than the smaller rank-friendly estimate, retain Roaring. Otherwise choose Sparse when its estimate is <= dense, including ties and empty input; else build Dense. Overflow in the Roaring comparison only disables that selection, whereas size-estimate overflow earlier returns an error. Physical-offset validation belongs to group construction; this private helper does not independently validate every bitmap offset for the Sparse/Roaring paths (rust/lance-core/src/utils/row_addr_remap.rs:417-441).

rank_if_present returns zero-based rank only for a present offset: Roaring contains then inclusive rank minus one, Sparse binary_search index, Dense specialized rank. is_empty tests container emptiness; Dense uses words.is_empty rather than a bit population check, but empty bitmap inputs select Sparse in the constructor. DeepSizeOf estimates Roaring with serialized_size and delegates vectors/dense owned children.

DenseRankedOffsets stores bit words and a u32 rank prefix per word. try_new allocates zeroed words, sets each offset bit, errors if its word index is outside the allocated words, then scans words collecting each preceding population count with checked u32 conversion. Prefix accumulation itself uses u64. The word bound alone would not reject an offset in unused bits of a final partial word; the group layout validator provides the exact physical bound.

Dense rank finds the containing word, rejects missing word or bit, and returns prefix + popcount(word & (bit-1)). There is no per-query scan or allocation. bit is a single nonzero u64 bit so bit-1 is defined, including bit63. Internal vectors must remain aligned. DeepSizeOf sums the two vectors with the same Context.

OldFragmentRemap is private group index, chosen retained-offset representation, preceding-retained-row count and optional physical row count. Only the rank representation has heap children. GroupRemap holds caller-ordered destination tuples (fragment ID, start rank u64, row count u32), with zero-row destinations omitted later. These structs derive Clone/Debug/PartialEq/Eq.

GroupRemap::new converts plain old IDs to (ID,None); new_with_layout converts physical counts to Some. Both delegate to the same shared constructor with group index, retained treemap and destination tuples. The plain path intentionally has no source offset bound.

new_with_old_frags walks destination tuples in caller order, skips zero-row destinations, appends (ID,current prefix,row count), and adds to total destination rows using ordinary u64 arithmetic. It clones the treemap bitmaps into an IntMap, collects old fragment metadata and creates a seen-fragment set. No destination-ID uniqueness or reserved-ID check occurs here; destination ranges are positional, so duplicate destination IDs can alias resulting physical addresses.

For each old fragment, reject duplicate IDs within the group, remove its retained bitmap or substitute empty, and if a physical count exists reject max retained offset >= physical rows. Build RankedOffsets with that bound, record group index/current retained prefix/count metadata and add retained length to the group prefix. Old fragment scan order is the input vector order, independent of IntMap iteration. Constructor failures discard local partially built state.

Reject retained addresses whose fragments were never listed (leftover per-fragment map), then require total new physical rows to equal treemap retained cardinality. Error messages include group/fragment or count context; leftover map key ordering is not a promised stable string order. Successful construction returns destination ranges and all old-fragment records, including fragments with no surviving rows. No separate validation proves destination address uniqueness.

compute_new_addr binary-searches destination start ranks, selecting the exact start or predecessor insertion index, then packs fragment ID and (rank-start) cast to u32 through RowAddress. No end check is performed here; construction cardinality plus a valid retained rank guarantees a destination exists and the offset fits that destination. Direct misuse of this private helper with an invalid rank could panic or truncate. GroupRemap DeepSizeOf measures the destination tuple vector.

Private IntHasher holds u64 state and derives Clone/Copy. Comments justify faster integer hashing for hot internal fragment IDs and explicitly warn that integer writes replace state, so composite keys can collide on their last integer field. The claim that production IDs are internal is an assumption here, not an input validation boundary. Default initializes FNV_OFFSET_BASIS=0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325 so the byte fallback distinguishes leading zero bytes.

Hasher::finish xors state with state>>32 to spread high bits down. Byte write performs wrapping FNV-1a multiplication by 0x0000_0100_0000_01b3. write_u32/write_u64 overwrite state with value times wrapping golden-ratio constant 0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15; write_usize casts and delegates. IntMap<K,V> aliases HashMap with BuildHasherDefault<IntHasher>; generic composite keys remain equality-correct but may collide heavily. HashMap iteration is not a source ordering contract.

CompactRemapStep privately owns group vector and integer-keyed old-fragment map. new creates each GroupRemap, inserts its old-fragment records and rejects any fragment appearing in multiple groups, then appends the group. Validation happens in local owned state before returning. Empty group input yields no groups; an explicitly supplied group with no old/new/retained rows still contributes one structural group.

new_with_layout repeats the group-build and cross-group duplicate check using physical row counts. It retains each group even when it contains no rows; this affects structural emptiness but not actual address lookups. Errors identify the duplicate fragment and current group.

CompactRemapStep::get extracts high32 fragment and low32 offset. Missing fragment returns outer None; an offset >= supplied physical rows also returns None. Missing retained offset inside a covered fragment returns Some(None). A present offset produces preceding-retained-count + zero-based rank, uses group_idx to locate its destination layout, and returns Some(Some(new address)). Without physical counts, every absent offset in a listed fragment is treated as deleted.

is_empty checks whether the group vector is empty. fully_deleted_fragments returns None if any old-fragment rank representation is nonempty; otherwise returns every old fragment ID. It proves all affected fragments deleted or gives no proof, never a partial subset. affected_fragments always returns all map keys. DeepSizeOf adds group vector and old-fragment map children.

Private RemapStep permits CompactRemapStep and Direct map inside a chain without adding a public RowAddrRemap variant. It derives Clone/Debug/PartialEq/Eq and delegates get/is_empty/affected/proof/DeepSizeOf. Direct get copies the stored optional value; only an empty Direct map can supply a fully-deleted proof, and all its key fragment IDs count as affected.

Public CompactRowAddrRemap has a private Vec<RemapStep>. Private new/new_with_layout each wrap one compact step, even if no groups exist. Private chained consumes remaps and flattens existing compact steps in sequence while wrapping each Direct map as a step. Top-level RowAddrRemap::chained already filters structurally empty inputs (rust/lance-core/src/utils/row_addr_remap.rs:91-103). This internal representation preserves the public enum shape.

Public CompactRowAddrRemap::get applies steps once in order to the current address. Missing lookup keeps the address and affected flag unchanged; deletion immediately returns Some(None); mapping updates current address and marks affected, even for an identity mapping. Final outer None means no step matched; otherwise Some(Some(final address)). A later step sees an earlier step's destination, and no earlier step is revisited. Address cycles cannot cause an unbounded loop because traversal is over the fixed step vector.

Private batch remapping loops over steps first, then mutable row positions. It skips None and absent lookups and writes present optional results. Terminal deletion remains None in later steps. This version-major ordering retains the same address semantics as individual chained get while keeping each step hot across the whole batch; no measured cache/performance guarantee is asserted.

Public is_empty requires every internal step structurally empty. affected_fragments unions every step's source fragment IDs, which can include intermediate rewrite versions. fully_deleted_fragments try-folds unions only while every step can prove all its affected fragments deleted; any step containing survivors or a nonempty Direct map returns None, even if the full chain ultimately deletes all original rows. DeepSizeOf delegates the steps vector.

The cfg(test) module imports proptest, and addr helper packs fragment/offset through RowAddress. Private ExpectedRankedOffsets distinguishes Sparse/Dense/Roaring. assert_layout_matches_legacy takes one source fragment's bitmap/physical count, destination tuples and expected rank representation; its oracle and checks follow below.

The helper collects old retained addresses in treemap order, flattens destination offsets in given order, zips them into an expected HashMap, constructs layout-aware compact remapping and inspects its private rank variant. It compares every physical source offset to expected retained/deleted behavior and checks the physical end offset and adjacent fragment are unaffected. This is a one-source-fragment oracle; it does not establish arbitrary multi-source scan ordering.

Sparse rank test uses offsets 1,63,511,9999 in a 10000-row universe, asserts Sparse, rejects missing zero and checks ranks 0 through 3. It crosses word boundaries without invoking dense representation.

Dense rank test inserts all offsets below 1024 except multiples of ten, asserts Dense, and compares every offset against expected presence and incrementing rank across words. Final rank equals retained cardinality.

Run-compressed test inserts range 100..9900 in a 10000-row universe, asserts Roaring and checks both excluded boundaries plus rank0/rank9799 endpoints. This verifies the representation decision for a contiguous run fixture, not all bitmap container types.

Three layout helper cases select Sparse (four offsets split across two destinations), Dense (1024-offset pattern with holes split at 400 retained rows), and Roaring (source offset run100..9900). The Roaring case serializes/deserializes a treemap without explicit optimize and uses destinations31 then30, preserving descending caller order. Each helper checks all source physical offsets and outside-boundary behavior.

Compact lookup fixture lists old fragments4 then3, with retained offsets4:{0,2,4},3:{0,1}; destinations10(2),11(0),12(3). A second group lists fragment7 with no survivors. Assertions cover five exact destinations, deleted holes, the all-deleted fragment and an uncovered fragment. Because plain compact has no physical layout, offset5 of fragment4 is also classified deleted; the fixture explicitly demonstrates this difference.

Fragment-set tests chain two wholly deleted fragment groups and expect both affected/proven-deleted unions. A group containing one surviving row plus another all-deleted source returns None for the full-deletion proof while affected_fragments retains both IDs. Chaining it with a deletion group still yields no all-deleted proof. The proof API is conservative and all-or-nothing.

A nonempty Direct map containing only one deletion cannot prove the whole source fragment deleted. Chaining two such partial Direct maps remains unable to prove full deletion and must leave unspecified source offsets unaffected; the tests explicitly check those missing entries.

An unknown retained fragment, even with balanced destination row count, is rejected by compact construction; the assertion checks is_err without error category/text. A separate ordering test sends two retained offsets to destinations12 then11 and asserts that exact caller-provided destination order.

Direct-map test includes arbitrary moved offset9,9, an explicit deletion and an unaffected neighboring offset, checks affected fragment IDs and nonempty status; empty() is structurally empty and returns outer None. No layout or count validation is expected from Direct.

Chained fixture first rewrites source0 offsets0/2 to fragment10 and deletes hole1, then keeps only fragment10 offset1 into fragment20. Source0 offset0 is deleted by the second step; offset1 by the first; offset2 reaches20. Uncovered fragment1 is unchanged. Batch assertions preserve existing None, delete both affected rows, map the survivor and keep an unaffected input.

int_hash_of builds a fresh default IntHasher. The hash test checks repeated scalar values and equal borrowed values hash equally, and requires >512 distinct low-11-bit buckets for each 1024-value strided/dense sample. This is a limited distribution assertion, not a benchmark or adversarial collision guarantee.

Composite-key test explicitly demonstrates equal hashes for integer tuples with identical last fields and for string/integer tuples ending in4. An IntMap of 48x48 integer pairs still stores and retrieves every distinct key and rejects absent keys, confirming equality resolves collisions. It does not establish acceptable performance for composite keys.

Forward/reverse insertion-order fixtures use seven source fragment IDs and one retained row each. They compare affected_fragments and fully_deleted_fragments only. They deliberately do not require row mappings to be independent of old fragment order: old order determines the concatenated scan stream. Preserve this narrow test claim when interpreting its broad test name.

Proptest generates 1–6 candidate fragment descriptors with dense, strided or wrapping-multiplied IDs, 1–23 physical rows each, a 144-element keep bitmap with probability0.75, and 1–4 positive destination gaps. Deduplication preserves first-seen old fragment order. The macro function uses proptest input strategies, not an ordinary callable public signature.

The property fixture walks old fragments in retained caller order and physical offsets ascending, records every covered address and the kept-address sequence, and excludes zero-survivor cases with prop_assume. It creates up to min(gaps,kept rows) destinations, distributes rows by quotient/remainder with earlier extra rows, and assigns IDs starting10000 with positive gaps. Every destination here has positive row count.

An independent Direct oracle maps the kept sequence into destination offsets, checks the sequence is exhausted and inserts explicit deletions for all other covered source rows. Plain compact lookup is compared against it for every covered address, two uncovered fragment IDs and affected-fragment sets. The property does not exercise compact_with_layout, out-of-physical-range offsets in affected fragments, all-deleted inputs, constructor errors or duplicate destination IDs. Module and macro close with no additional production definitions.

files.role: Public in-memory primitives and a private dense-counts byte codec for stable-partition row mapping: CountsMatrix, streaming builder, prefix rank, point translation and sweep translation. Labels are destination-list indices, not fragment IDs. Production label-column IO/cache ownership is outside this module. Private state prevents ordinary direct mutation but decode deliberately separates structural decoding from semantic count validation.
files.limits: All 697 lines and local tests were inspected; none were executed. The comments locate label IO/cache responsibilities in lance-index, whose implementation remains pending. Do not infer a released stable file-format contract or dataset-version gate from this helper's local codec version1. Full FRI schema/reader selection and whether callers always call validate are unknown. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/stable_partition.rs:4-60; rust/lance-core/src/utils/stable_partition.rs:74-82; rust/lance-core/src/utils/stable_partition.rs:191-290) Local tests omit wrong-version decoding, excess live-row budgets, maximum destination count/overflow, short validity buffers and empty/excess-input sweeps. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/stable_partition.rs:484-697)
ranges: License and design for reordered rewrites: one nullable u16 destination label per old physical row in caller scan order; NULL means deleted. Rows may interleave among destinations but each destination must preserve relative source order. Parallel writers must merge their output in that order. Arbitrary within-destination permutations cannot be represented by these labels alone and require explicit final offsets in another format. This is a correctness precondition rather than a runtime test here.

Cumulative counts are stored per destination at each fixed-size block end. Point translation combines count before the block with within-block exclusive prefix rank; a sequential sweep seeds all counters at a block boundary and increments by label. The block is also the documented label IO/cache unit, but that IO belongs to lance-index and is not implemented here. Approximate dense-grid footprint examples omit header/Vec overhead; exact payload size is ceil(total_rows/block_rows)*num_destinations*4. Imports supply core DeepSizeOf/Error/Result and Arrow NullBuffer.

Public defaults: DEFAULT_BLOCK_ROWS=64*1024 (65536), MAX_DESTINATIONS=u16::MAX+1 (65536). Private codec constants: magic LSPC, version1, fixed28-byte header, representation0 for dense little-endian u32 grid; unknown future tags are rejected. corrupt wraps messages as CorruptFile named stable_partition_counts. These local codec constants are not proof of a Lance dataset format version or released stability designation.

Public CountsMatrix derives Clone/Debug/PartialEq/Eq with private destination count, block rows, total old physical rows u64 (including deleted), and row-major cumulative Vec<u32>. Each matrix row is through the end of a block, unlike the exclusive count-before accessor. Deleted counts are implicit differences from physical row budgets.

Accessors return stored dimensions; num_blocks divides cumulative cell count by destination count, relying on construction/decode shape checks. block_of divides an arbitrary row by block_rows and casts to usize without range validation. block_range computes start=block*block_rows and end=min(start+block_rows,total_rows), with ordinary arithmetic and no bounds check: an invalid block can yield start>end or overflow. Private block_row slices the flattened grid and panics if its indices are invalid.

count_before(block,label) returns0 for block0 without label validation, otherwise indexes the preceding matrix row. counters_at_block similarly returns a newly allocated zero vector for block0 or clones the previous row. Both permit the end boundary block==num_blocks on a valid matrix; they do not return Result and callers own bounds validation.

total(label) returns0 for an empty matrix without checking the label, otherwise indexes the last row. total_live_rows sums that final row as u64 or returns0. deleted_through(block) subtracts the current cumulative live sum from the block end; it assumes valid monotonic/budget counts and a valid block. Using malformed decoded counts before validate can underflow ordinary arithmetic.

validate iterates all blocks, rejects any label count that decreases from the previous block, and rejects the increase in total live rows if it exceeds the current physical block length. It returns contextual CorruptFile through corrupt; O(blocks*destinations) scanning is why decode does not do this automatically. Private shape invariants ensure complete matrix rows; validation does not compare counts against the actual label column or destination fragment metadata.

encode reserves header+cells*4 bytes and writes LSPC, version1, repr0, destination count, block_rows as little-endian u32, total_rows as little-endian u64, then every cumulative u32 in row-major order. Header offsets are0,4,8,12,16,20; payload begins28. It does not call validate or return Result; capacity arithmetic is unchecked in source.

decode first requires28 bytes, rejects wrong magic, unsupported version and representation tags other than0 via CorruptFile. It then extracts destination count, block rows and total rows from little-endian fields. Header fields use exact byte slices after the length check, so their array conversions are structurally guarded.

decode calls check_shape before division; invalid destination count or zero block rows yields InvalidInput, despite being read from persisted bytes. It computes ceil(total_rows/block_rows), checks block-count*destinations*4 for overflow and exact equality with remaining bytes, rejecting truncation and trailing bytes as CorruptFile. It reserves/reads the grid as u32 little-endian chunks and returns without validate. Structural success alone does not prove monotonic counts or per-block row budgets.

Private check_shape accepts destination counts1..=65536 and any positive block_rows; it returns descriptive InvalidInput otherwise. check_label compares a u16 label as u32 against destination count and also returns InvalidInput. The maximum valid label is65535; the default block size is advisory, not enforced.

CountsMatrix DeepSizeOf reports cumulative Vec capacity times sizeof(u32), excluding inline storage already accounted by the trait convention. Public CountsMatrixBuilder derives Debug with private shape, per-destination running u32 counters, cumulative cells, total physical-row count and rows-in-current-block. No shared mutable/concurrent state is exposed.

try_new validates shape, allocates zeroed running counters for each destination, initializes cumulative empty and both physical-row counters zero. Empty input is valid and will produce zero matrix rows at finish.

push accepts one Option<u16> per old physical row. For Some, reject out-of-range label and checked per-destination u32 increment overflow before advancing any physical counters; None only advances physical counters. total_rows increments as ordinary u64. When rows_in_block reaches block_rows, append a full snapshot of all running counters and reset rows_in_block to zero. A destination can hold at most u32::MAX rows, whose last zero-based offset is u32::MAX-1; this builder cannot represent count2^32.

finish consumes the builder, appends one final cumulative row only when the last block is partial, and moves cumulative/shape/total fields into CountsMatrix. Exact block multiples get no extra row; empty input keeps zero rows. No secondary validation pass occurs.

Public rank_label_prefix counts matching label values strictly before upto, ignoring positions invalid in NullBuffer. If validity is absent or reports no nulls, it skips per-element validity checks. Slicing values[..upto] enforces bounds by panic, not Result; no validity-length check exists, and counts cast usize to u32. In intended blocks limited to u32 rows the count fits; an arbitrary standalone oversized slice could truncate. Work is linear in prefix length with no output allocation.

translate_in_block first derives block length via block_range, then returns InvalidInput if values length differs or position is outside it. It does not separately validate the block index before block_range arithmetic. A supplied validity buffer is not length-checked. These checks establish the requested values slice size and position, not consistency of counts and labels.

For an invalid/NULL position return Ok(None) before reading or validating the underlying label, so arbitrary null payload values are allowed. Otherwise validate that label, compute count_before(block,label)+rank_label_prefix(values,validity,pos,label) using ordinary u32 addition, and return (label,offset). There is no destination-fragment-ID lookup, comparison with final destination totals, or validation that every supplied prefix label matches the stored counts.

Public SweepTranslator derives Debug and privately owns a Vec<u32> of per-destination counters. new rejects start_block >= max(num_blocks,1), allowing block0 for an empty matrix but not the end boundary for a nonempty matrix. It seeds counters from CountsMatrix::counters_at_block; only a block boundary is expressible.

advance(None) returns None and changes no counter. Some(label) checks counter-vector bounds, returns the old counter as offset and increments with ordinary u32 addition, unlike the builder's checked increment. It tracks neither processed physical rows nor remaining dataset length: an empty or exhausted sweep can accept further valid labels. Caller must feed the correct ordered row stream and avoid overflow; no matrix consistency validation happens here.

Tests use seeded StdRng and Rng/SeedableRng traits and NullBuffer. random_labels makes a NULL with probability1/8, otherwise a uniform destination label. build uses the public builder and unwraps each valid fixture operation. These helpers are local; runtime tests were not executed during KB analysis.

reference independently assigns monotonically increasing offsets per label using HashMap counters, preserving NULL positions. block_slices turns optional labels into a values vector with 0xBEEF garbage at NULL positions and creates a validity buffer only if any null exists. This explicitly tests null payload exclusion instead of relying on zero fill.

Hand example uses labels[0,2,NULL,2,1,1,0,2,NULL,0], three destinations and blocks of four. It validates the matrix, expects three blocks for ten physical rows and range8..10 for the last, and checks exclusive count-before values including the legal block3 end boundary.

The same fixture asserts destination totals3/2/3, total live8, deleted-through prefixes1 then2 and counters at block1=[1,0,2]. Exact first-eight-row input produces two blocks; empty input has zero blocks/rows/live/label totals and validates. These tests distinguish partial-final, exact-multiple and empty layouts.

Round trip uses seed7,1000 rows,five destinations,block64 and compares decoded equality before validate; empty also round-trips. Short bytes, corrupt magic, a one-byte truncation and repr9 fail decoding. A manually decreased cumulative cell is encoded and decoded successfully, then fails validate, demonstrating the intentional separation. Test assertions mostly check is_err, not exact categories/messages.

Builder rejects zero destinations, destination count aboveMAX_DESTINATIONS, zero block size and out-of-range label3 for m3; valid label2 then succeeds. The test does not assert exact error variants/messages, state after failed push or u32 counter overflow.

Seed42 fixture has1000 rows,five destinations,block64. Every point translation across every block is compared with the independent per-label reference using garbage null payloads; sweeps beginning at every valid block boundary are compared over the entire remaining label stream. This verifies point/sweep order agreement on one seeded mixed-null input, not arbitrary within-destination permutation support.

Input checks use one four-row block and assert errors for wrong values length, out-of-range position, live label9 for m2, invalid sweep block1 and advance label9. Although a comment calls an out-of-range data label corruption, check_label actually returns InvalidInput (rust/lance-core/src/utils/stable_partition.rs:306-314). Short validity buffers, overflow and extra sweep input are not tested here; module ends.
